submission.text: will have one RD wide BAA to monitor on SAM.gov instead of multiple BAAs across the Directorate • Why do we need another contracting tool separate from DETER? • Selecting the right contracting tool for the job leads to the best outcomes. TACTICAL BAA fills a gap for pursuing FAR-based awards for 6.1-6.4 efforts that was not available previously at the directorate level. TACTICAL will complement other tools such as the DETER ARA, SBIR/STTRs, and grants & cooperative agreements under the upcoming RAD Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA). • What if a technically qualified offeror wants to join a Topic Area Group, but missed the normal deadline? • The offeror can either wait and submit during the next annual period (every January) or AFRL can choose to release an interim request for additional executive summaries. • Will these slides be available online or via email? •The slide will be emailed to all registered participants, along with the Q&A, and will also be posted to the sam.gov DETER Virtual Industry Day announcement. • When will the next closed call be released? •Please keep monitoring the TACTICAL SAM.gov posting and sign up for notification of changes. This will notify you when there are changes or a Call announcement is made under TACTICAL. AFRL-2023-4752 Approved

BEP's objective is to procure contractor services to manage, operate, maintain supplies and perform maintenance and provide technical support for the Wastewater and Storm Water Programs. The WWPP requires services to support the BEP on a 24/7 basis. The WWPP currently consists of four (4) systems: (1) Wiping Solution Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WSWPP), (2) Plating Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (PWPP), (3) Grease Trap Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (GTWPP), and (4) Wiping Solution Recycling Plant (WSRP). The WWPP includes an on-site lab and a materials storage area. Refer to Attachments 2, 3, 4, and 5 for descriptions of the four (4) systems as well as Attachment 9 and 10 for listings of the equipment that are part of the WSWPP and PWPP, respectively. The GTWPP may be removed during the course of this contract. In addition to these systems, additional systems are currently being researched that will be included in the scope of this requirement. TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENTS: The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Advanced Research Announcement (ARA) for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to enable the rapid integration of Systems of Systems (SoS) and the auto generation of tests of the System-of-systems Technology Integration Tool Chain for Heterogeneous Electronic Systems (STITCHES) subsystem specifications and properties. White papers shall: Describe methods to develop, implement, and demonstrate a software prototype of a SoS that will provide increased military effectiveness, cost leverage (i.e., the cost of the opponent to counter relative to the cost of the U.S. to deploy), and adaptability relative to the current platform-centric approach; Outline the development and provide a system architecting approach to achieve rapid integration of new U.S. technologies as they are developed, without requiring significant re-engineering of existing capabilities, systems, or systems of systems; Outline how to implement applicable Open System Architect

operate (ATO) issued by the Department of Defense (DoD); Provide system-level user identity and access management, and application-level single sign-on (SSO); Establish a repository and backup and restore all ecosystem data; Develop a graphical user interface system for web-based utilization of the toolchain and users with limited toolchain experience; and Design, implement, and integrate secure cloud-based hosting in multiple levels and provide the ability for the secure transfer of files between different levels.
